name: Ritenour High School
notes: Continuous high-school entity: first four-year program enrolled ten freshmen in fall 1914 (classes in the Ritenour/Overland grade-school building, now ALL-304); first graduating class May 17, 1918. Dedicated building opened September 1924 on Forest Avenue (ALL-303); moved to the current 9100 St. Charles Rock Road campus for the 1950-51 term (21.5-acre site purchased 1935; $630K bond approved December 1946; Class of 1951 first to graduate there). Seed's '1927' is unverified and likely conflates a later milestone; Wikipedia lists 'Established 1911' based on earlier HS-level coursework (first-year-equivalent studies began 1910 per State ex rel. Bender v. Hackmann, Mo. 1922). School still operating. Physical ZIP is 63114 (Breckenridge Hills); seed's 63074 reflects served community.

name: Ritenour Middle School
notes: Occupies the original 1924 Ritenour High School building (8740 Forest Ave; same site as ALL-303). Became the district's first junior high when the new high school opened for the 1950-51 term — the district hired James A. Painter as its first junior-high principal in May 1950 in anticipation. Became a middle school in 1981 when sixth graders moved up from elementaries and ninth graders moved to the high school. The 1923-built portion was demolished in 1991 and replaced. Still operating. Seed ZIP 63074 is served-community; physical address 2500 Marshall Ave is 63114.

name: DeHart School
historical_names: Lewis DeHart Eight Room Elementary School
notes: Land at St. Charles Rock Road & Wismer Avenue (Breckenridge Hills) offered by the DeHart sisters in November 1943 and purchased early 1944 ($1,000-$2,600 across three deeds) with reverter conditions requiring a school for white children named the 'Lewis DeHart School,' honoring their father, a Ritenour board member/president 1889-1900. Building bid ($97,685) accepted August 1944; completed 1945. Closed after the 1979-80 year per the district's own history ('closed in 1980'); the 1983 Missouri Court of Appeals opinion in DeHart v. Ritenour Consolidated School District (663 S.W.2d 332) records classes 'from 1945 until 1981' — a one-year discrepancy, likely school-year vs. record-year. Property sold 1988; demolished for Centennial Bank, which holds a memorial plaque (dedicated September 8, 1988) and a cornerstone time capsule was recovered. Receiving school not identified. Seed ZIP 63074 is served-community; physical location is Breckenridge Hills, 63114.

name: Iveland Elementary School
notes: Resolved seed's '1940s': the school's own history page records a four-acre site bought with February 1928 bond funds ($8,000) and a permanent one-story four-room building built in 1936 (a WPA-era project per the district history; sight-saving classes had run in a portable on the site from 1935). Principal Lillian Kegelman served 1936-1969. Additions 1949, 1956, 1964, and post-1990 rebuild. Still operating at 1836 Dyer Ave. Seed ZIP 63074 is served-community; physical ZIP is 63114 (Overland).

name: Buck School
notes: One-room log cabin built 1846 near Woodson and Lackland roads on land donated by Elizabeth Smith; first teacher Thomas W. Goldie at $20/month. In 1867 it joined a nearby temporary school for Negro children to form the rural Ritenour district and took the name Ritenour School — that is the 'closed' date, an identity change rather than a shutdown (district states the lineage explicitly: Buck School -> Ritenour School -> Overland School -> Old Overland School -> Administrative Center; successor row ALL-321 'Ritenour School' lives in another batch). The original log building was destroyed by fire December 28, 1886 (board minutes attribute it to a flue defect, not the often-retold Christmas-tree myth) and was replaced by a two-room brick building completed summer 1887 for $2,245. Seed's 'closed unknown' resolved.

name: Lackland Avenue School
historical_names: Lackland Avenue School for Negro children
notes: Frame 16'x24' schoolhouse on Lackland Avenue (at Sims Avenue, Overland) built on land purchased August 1888 ($2,000); opened the second Monday in October 1888 as the district's school for Negro children. On August 12, 1913 the board designated it the site of a high-school class for Negro students — the first for African-American pupils in St. Louis County. The board voted shortly before the end of 1915 to close it and consolidate operations with the new Elmwood building (ALL-292); the building was sold June 1917 for $65. Seed's '1900s' opening corrected to 1888; seed's 1915 close and the Lackland->Elmwood merge both confirmed by the district's commissioned history and its 100 Facts page.

name: Elmwood Park School
notes: District's school for African-American children in the Elmwood Park subdivision (Chicago Heights Blvd & Dielman Rd). Began as a rented 'branch school' whose classes started December 4, 1899 (Block 9, Robertson Street); later housed in the Elmwood Park Baptist Church (through May 1912) and the rented 'Fisher place' before the permanent building — funded by the April 15, 1915 bond issue (227-108) — was built starting June 1915 and absorbed the Lackland Avenue School that year. Remained an all-Black school even after district-wide integration began in 1958; an HEW directive forced a plan (implemented ~1974-75) that divided Elmwood students among Wyland, New Overland (ALL-308, another batch) and Iveland (ALL-289) schools and moved the Vo-Prep program into the Elmwood building. 'Closed' recorded as 1975 (last classes under that dispersal; the district history says both the Elmwood building and the original Vo-Prep building were sold in summer 1976 — exact final year could be 1975 or 1976). Seed's '1900s' open and 'unknown' close both resolved. No single successor — students were dispersed per the HEW plan.

name: Holy Trinity School
district_operator: Holy Trinity Parish / Archdiocese of St. Louis
notes: SEED ERROR: 'Closed 2024' is actually the date Ritenour School District purchased the property (closed August 13/20, 2024, $1 million, for its Center for Educational Excellence) — the school itself closed at the end of the 2018-19 year (127 students, enrollment down 67% since 2002), per the St. Louis Review; the Archdiocese announcement is dated April 2019. Holy Trinity School was itself established in 2002 as a consolidation of St. William, St. Kevin, St. Gregory and All Souls parish schools (opened K-8 with 382 students), occupying the former St. Kevin School building at 10901 St. Henry Lane; it also absorbed Our Lady of the Presentation (Overland) students when that school closed in 2009. Parish itself closed June 2020. No successor school — students dispersed. For pre-2002 coverage of this site, the predecessor parish schools (St. Kevin, St. Gregory, St. William, All Souls) deserve their own rows if not already batched.

name: Hope Lutheran School - St. Ann
notes: SEED CORRECTION: seed status 'Current/Unknown' is stale — privateschoolreview lists the school as 'Closed 2016' after continuous operation since 1943 (its own profile text; a directory listing also says 'Since 1943'). The sponsoring congregation, Hope Lutheran Church (joined LCMS December 31, 1945 per the LCMS church locator; IRS exemption July 1941), remains active at 10701 St. Cosmas Lane. Single aggregating source for both dates — mark probable and corroborate via MO DESE nonpublic records or Missouri District LCMS reports if precision matters.

name: American Trade School
notes: For-profit HVAC/electrical trade school at 3925 Industrial Drive; BBB records business start July 1, 2003 and incorporation July 25, 2003, consistent with LinkedIn and tradeschoolsreview 'founded 2003.' ACCSC-accredited. Still operating. As the seed notes, unlikely to produce traditional yearbooks — low value for the archive survey.

name: Olivet University - St. Louis Campus
notes: Olivet University (evangelical institution founded as Olivet Theological College & Seminary in 2000, incorporated as a university 2004 in California) established its St. Ann campus at 10257 St. Charles Rock Road circa 2023 — a City of St. Ann special-use permit for 'a Bible College' at the address (property owner Jonathan Park) was heard April 24, 2023, noting the site was 'Formerly Brookes Bible College.' Olivet now lists St. Ann as its MAIN campus and held its first Missouri convocation there in September 2026. The building itself opened May 2014 as Brookes Bible College (a separate, now-closed institution worth its own seed row if not already covered). Olivet had a St. Louis extension site by the late 2010s per Wikipedia. Low yearbook value.

name: St. Ann School District
historical_names: Historical St. Ann public school district
notes: LIKELY PHANTOM DISTRICT: found no evidence an independent 'St. Ann School District' ever existed. The city of St. Ann was platted by developer Charles Vatterott beginning 1943 and incorporated in 1948 — recent enough that it never formed its own district; it has always been served by the Ritenour School District (which covered much of the area since 1867 and annexed Scudder District territory in 1940 and 1949) and the Pattonville R-3 district. Schools physically in St. Ann included Pattonville's St. Ann Elementary (seed row ALL-174, another batch), Ritenour's DeHart and Iveland elementaries, and the parochial schools. A 1943 Vatterott letter to the Ritenour board proposing a 'St. Ann's Public School' shows Ritenour already being treated as the area's district before the city existed. Recommend retaining only as a search alias; a human could confirm via DESE historical district directories or St. Louis County recorder records that no St. Ann district was ever organized.

name: Ritenour Consolidated School District
notes: ADMINISTRATIVE DISTRICT — no yearbook of its own; Track B should target member schools. Timeline (district's commissioned history 'Ritenour: Our First 132 Years' + Missouri Supreme Court in State ex rel. Bender v. Hackmann, 1922, and MoHistory's 1926 commencement-program record, which both style it 'Ritenour Consolidated School District'): rural district formed 1867 by joining Buck School and a temporary Negro school (named for landowner J.S. Ritenour); reorganized as a village district with a six-member board April 1907; 'Consolidated' in use by 1921-22 litigation — seed's 'organized as a consolidated district in 1910' is unverified and likely conflates 1910, the year the district began first-year high-school coursework per the court opinion. Seed's note that land was added from the Scudder District in 1940 and 1949 is corroborated by the district history. Member schools include, in this batch: Ritenour HS (ALL-285), Ritenour Middle/Junior High (ALL-287), DeHart (ALL-288), Iveland (ALL-289), Lackland (ALL-291), Elmwood (ALL-292); in other batches: Ritenour School (ALL-321), Overland School (ALL-309), New Overland (ALL-308), Scudder Avenue School (ALL-392); plus unbatched/unnamed: Home Heights, Midland, Marion, Marvin, Kratz, Wyland, Buder, Ashby, Hoech Junior High, Ritenour School for Early Childhood Education. Still operating; NCES District ID 1931680.

name: Ritenour High School - Forest Avenue Campus
historical_names: Ritenour Senior High School (Forest Ave building)
notes: Ritenour's first dedicated high-school building at 8740 Forest Avenue (Charlack site — parts of Blocks 35-36 purchased March 1921 from Edward Gocke; $65K bond approved May 1921, re-approved October 1921, bonds sold March 1923, cornerstone laid July 1923, designed with input from William B. Ittner's firm). Opened September 1924 for the 1924-25 year; served as the senior high until the new St. Charles Rock Road campus (ALL-285) opened for the 1950-51 term, then became the district's first junior high — the same building is today's Ritenour Middle School (ALL-287) at 2500 Marshall Ave. The 1923-built portion was demolished in 1991. Kept as a separate row per the no-silent-merge campus rule.

name: Ritenour High School - Old Overland Campus
notes: High-school program housed inside the district's main grade school at 2420 Woodson Road — the 1907 eight-room building erected on the site of the earlier Ritenour School (Buck School site; the building is separately seeded as ALL-309 'Overland School'). The Missouri Supreme Court in State ex rel. Bender v. Hackmann (1922) records that the 1907 building, erected for grade-school purposes, began housing 'first-year high-school course' studies in 1910, added second-year studies 1914 and third/fourth-year by 1916 — seed's '1918' conflates the first graduating class (May 17, 1918). The high school moved to the new Forest Avenue building (ALL-303) in September 1924. The Woodson Road building continued as the Overland/New Overland elementary and is today the district Administrative Center.
